Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1111); Balak, a Moabite:--Balac.
BiblicalUsage: Balak's name reaches the New Testament in the risen Christ's letter to Pergamos. There He says the church holds the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Balak matters because he tried to buy a curse against God's people and could not, yet his name still warns us: a king who cannot curse Israel can still tempt her, and temptation did what cursing could not.
